title: Matrix Factorization for Recommenders
interviewAnswer: Matrix factorization learns low-dimensional user and item vectors whose interaction predicts preference. With implicit feedback, objectives often weight observed interactions plus sampled/unobserved examples.
keyPoints: Bias terms and confidence weighting matter.
why: Matrix Factorization for Recommenders appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Matrix factorization learns low-dimensional user and item vectors whose interaction predicts preference. With implicit feedback, objectives often weight observed interactions plus sampled/unobserved examples. Regularization handles sparse data. Bias terms and confidence weighting matter. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Learn 64-dimensional user/item embeddings and rank items by dot product.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Matrix Factorization for Recommenders make?
How would you validate or debug Matrix Factorization for Recommenders in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.

lab.goal: Factorize a tiny user-item rating matrix with gradient descent.
lab.buildIt:
import numpy as np
rng=np.random.default_rng(0)
R=np.array([[5.,4.,0.],[0.,3.,4.],[4.,0.,5.]])
mask=R>0; U=rng.normal(scale=.1,size=(3,2)); V=rng.normal(scale=.1,size=(3,2))
for _ in range(2000):
    E=(U@V.T-R)*mask
    U-=.01*(E@V+.01*U); V-=.01*(E.T@U+.01*V)
print(U@V.T)
lab.shipIt: At scale, separate offline factor training from low-latency candidate retrieval, exclude already-seen/ineligible items and monitor popularity/exposure bias.
